headline: Highest risk is data leakage: EMQX has broad egress and HTTP API exposure, while ai-engineering-hub is an unverified docs-only agent with no stated isolation or provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can surface agent/MCP/RAG content and B exposes an HTTP API, so a plausible instruction-hijack path exists if B ingests A’s outputs or shared files. Neither profile documents provenance tracking or isolation. This is not proven by evidence, but uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text from a shared file, queue, or API payload without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the pair is connected through a manual copy-paste bridge, prompt injection risk remains limited but present.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B.
Add a provenance tag to every A-produced artifact.
Require human review before B acts on any A-generated instruction.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B has broad network egress and touches IoT data, while A is an unverified docs-only agent with no declared data classes or isolation. If they share a workspace or context, B could transmit A-derived content off-host. The profiles do not prove a leak, but the default egress posture makes the pathway plausible.
conditions: IF A and B share files or prompts containing sensitive content, B can exfiltrate that content via network egress.
IF B is configured to forward full context to its backend or APIs, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Block B egress except to approved endpoints.
Avoid placing sensitive data in shared prompts or files.
Rotate any secrets that were already shared across the pair.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write surface and B only exposes HTTP API calls, so overlapping mutable-resource writes are not documented. The pair may still contend if an external orchestrator maps A outputs into B API actions, but that is not shown here. With no shared write target, conflict stays low.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same downstream API resource, conflicts can occur.
IF A is extended with filesystem or database write permissions, overlap risk increases.
mitigations: Assign distinct API credentials per agent.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Keep A read-only.
Document ownership of each mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A’s outputs can plausibly feed B, and B has an HTTP API plus broad egress, so unverified A content could be operationalized by B. The profiles do not show explicit verification gates or downstream action limits. Because B can act externally, the cascade can affect multiple work products, not just a single document.
conditions: IF B treats A-generated text as authoritative input, cascading errors can propagate to external actions.
IF A produces incorrect facts or instructions and B forwards them via API, the error becomes operational.
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against a second source.
Add a human approval step before any B action.
Log and diff A inputs versus B actions.
Limit B to read-only or dry-run mode.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: B touches IoT data and has broad egress, while A’s docs-only profile does not specify residency or retention controls. If EU or regulated IoT data flows through A into B, the mismatch could create a compliance gap. The evidence is indirect, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is routed from A into B, retention and residency obligations may diverge.
IF B stores or forwards data outside the required jurisdiction, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it.
Keep regulated data out of shared prompts.
Confirm residency and retention settings for B.
Record a data-processing inventory for the pair.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
